timer_toggle_auto_start_work_desc: Automatically begin the next work session after a break ends.
timer_toggle_auto_start_break_desc: Automatically begin a break when a work session ends.
timer_toggle_short_breaks_desc: Skip the short break between work rounds.
timer_toggle_long_breaks_desc: Skip the long break at the end of each cycle.
timer_toggle_countdown_desc: Arc starts full and subtracts as time passes.
notif_toggle_desktop_desc: Show a system notification when each round ends.
notif_toggle_tick_work_desc: Play a ticking sound during work sessions.
notif_toggle_tick_break_desc: Play a ticking sound during break sessions.
system_toggle_autostart_desc: Start Pomotroid automatically when you sign in.
system_toggle_aot_desc: Keep the timer window above all other windows.
system_toggle_break_aot_desc: Disable always-on-top while a break is running.
system_toggle_show_tray_desc: Display a persistent icon in the system tray.
system_tray_gnome_hint: On GNOME, tray icons require the AppIndicator extension. Install it with your package manager (e.g. gnome-shell-extension-appindicator) or from extensions.gnome.org, then log out and back in.
system_toggle_min_tray_desc: Hide the window to the tray when minimized.
system_toggle_close_tray_desc: Hide to the tray instead of quitting when the window is closed.
system_toggle_websocket_desc: Expose a local WebSocket endpoint for external integrations (port {port}).
system_toggle_check_updates_desc: Automatically check for new versions when Settings is opened.
shortcuts_accessibility_notice: Global shortcuts require Accessibility access on macOS. Enable Pomotroid in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
shortcuts_note: Global shortcuts work even when the window is not focused. Click a field and press your desired key combination to record it.
shortcuts_toggle_enabled_desc: Register system-wide keyboard shortcuts for controlling the timer.
shortcuts_local_note: Active while the app window is focused. Click a field and press a key to rebind.
advanced_toggle_verbose_logging_desc: Enable detailed debug logging to help diagnose issues.
about_reset_confirm: This will reset all settings to defaults.
stats_empty_history: Complete your first session to see your history
notification_work_body: Time to get back to work. You've got this!
notification_work_start_body: Time to focus. You've got this!
notification_short_break_body: Take a short break. Stretch, breathe, relax.
notification_long_break_body: You've earned a long break. Step away and recharge.
tooltip_restart_round: Restart the current round from the beginning.
tooltip_reset: Reset the timer to the first work round. Current session progress will be cleared.
tooltip_round_counter: Current work round out of the total rounds before a long break.
tooltip_round_counter_session: Continuous session round count. Resets only when the timer is reset.
tooltip_verbose_logging: Enables detailed debug logging. Use when reporting issues. Log files are accessible via Open Log Folder in Settings → About.
tooltip_dial_countdown: When enabled, the progress arc counts down to zero instead of filling up.
tooltip_auto_start_work: Automatically start the next work round when a break ends.
tooltip_auto_start_break: Automatically start the break when a work round completes.
tooltip_websocket: Enables a local WebSocket server for external integrations such as stream overlays. Disabled by default.
notif_pool_note: One of these plays each time, never the same one twice in a row.
notif_pool_note_tick: The tick always uses the first of these. It fires every second, so varying it would be noise rather than variety.
notif_alert_note: Pick a bundled sound or choose your own audio file. A custom file always takes priority over the preset.
customize_layout_desc: Drag the parts of the timer above or below the clock, or into Hidden to leave them out. The clock window changes as you go. On a narrow window the timer keeps only the clock whatever the layout says.
customize_colors_desc: Changes show in every window as you make them and are kept only when you save. Saving under a built-in theme's name customises that theme; deleting the customised copy brings the original back.
customize_theme_name_too_long: A theme name can be at most {max} characters.
customize_theme_overrides: This will customise the built-in "{name}" theme.
customize_hex_invalid: Colours must be hex values such as #2f384b.
appearance_clock_style_desc: The ring suits a plain window but draws a circle across the middle of a background image. The other styles trade how quickly the time reads against how much of the picture stays visible.
appearance_clock_digital: Large digits with a progress bar
appearance_clock_analog: Clock face with a pie of time left
appearance_font_digits_desc: The digits are listed separately because figures that are not all the same width make the time shift sideways every second. A font whose numbers line up is worth choosing here even when the interface uses another.
appearance_window_opacity_desc: Make the window see-through so what is behind it stays readable. The dial and its text keep their colours. Turning it on or back off takes effect after a restart, and a see-through window uses the app's own titlebar instead of the native frame.
appearance_bg_toggle_desc: Draw the chosen image behind the timer as a backdrop.
appearance_bg_framing_hint: Drag the preview to choose which part of the image shows. Scroll or pinch to zoom.
appearance_bg_shuffle_desc: Walk the folder in a random order. Off follows file names, so numbering them sets the order. Either way every picture is shown before any repeats.
appearance_bg_rotate_round_desc: Change the background when focus and break swap.
appearance_bg_rotate_mins_desc: Changes the picture on a clock, whether or not the timer is running. Double-click the timer to change it by hand at any time.
connect_note: Pair this device with Pomotroid on your computer over Wi-Fi. Open Settings → System on the desktop, enable phone connections and scan the QR code. While connected, this device follows the desktop timer and its settings.
connect_remote_banner: Following the desktop timer — settings apply to {name}.
system_toggle_lan_desc: Let the Pomotroid app on your phone pair with this computer over Wi-Fi.
system_lan_adapter_desc: Which network adapter the QR code and link point at. Pick the one your phone is on if the automatic choice lands on a VM, VPN or Docker adapter.
system_lan_note: Scan this code from the phone app (Settings → Desktop → Scan QR Code) or open the link in the phone's browser. Windows may ask to allow Pomotroid through the firewall the first time.
info_task_choose: Choose the task for this round
notification_overtime_body: Keep going, or start your break when you're ready.
focus_preset_full: You can keep up to {max} presets.
focus_presets_desc: Click a preset to switch all durations and the rounds before a long break at once. Saving under an existing name replaces that preset.
focus_goal_desc: Progress shows under the timer, with the time you will reach it. The streak counts the days in a row that met the goal.
focus_flow_desc: When a focus round ends, keep counting instead of moving on. Start your break when you are ready; the time you actually spent is recorded.
focus_notes_desc: When a focus round ends, offer a line to write down what you got done. The notes appear in Statistics.
focus_sound_breaks_desc: Keep the sound going through breaks too.
focus_sound_desc: Plays while a round is running and stops when the timer is paused. The sounds are generated on the fly, so they never repeat; your own file loops.
focus_sound_web: The focus sound plays on the desktop you are connected to.
